title: Rescued kayaker gives safety advice
description: Gary Pierce, a kayaker from Winthrop, Massachusetts, talks about safety precautions kayakers should take. Pierce was rescued by the Coast Guard in October of 2017 in Boston Harbor after he was beset by weather.  (U.S Coast Guard video by Petty Officer Andrew Barresi)
keywords: kayak, life jackets, boston harbor, canoe, Wear It, Safe Boating, Paddle Board, Coast Guard, rescue, USCG, Boston

transcript.text: - I, well I felt like I was gonna be a father still.
Which is a weird thought to have at that moment, but...
So I have two sons, Calison and Jack,
and that's who I'd said goodbye to.
And so the moment they picked me up and put me in the boat,
they were so calm and so just sure of themselves,
that I wanted to let them know, like,
you just reunited me with my children.
(guitar music)
I think that there's actually way more things
I could have done, so my list will be very short
of the things I did correctly,
but first and foremost, I think just even with my peers,
giving them the map and the directions
of where I was gonna be headed.
I took a picture and then I edited the photo
so I could show him exactly the route that I was going.
^- He filed a float plan with some friends and relatives
^before he left.
It's just a summary of where he plans on taking his boat,
how long he plans on being out,
and when and where he plans on returning.
So that if he doesn't arrive on time,
we have an idea of where to search for him
or that he's missing at all.
^- When he was in trouble, the first thing he did
^was call 9-1-1.
^He maintained continuous comms with us
here in the command center, and he even used his cell phone
as a signaling device.
- He was able to talk to Sector Boston directly
and help vector us into his position
so that we could locate him and rescue him.
So he had a difficult time using his cell phone
to contact us because it was wet.
If he had had a handheld marine radio
or something like that to signal us at night,
it might have been a lot easier to find him,
it might have been less of a dire situation for him.
- The very first thing did when I got home
is I Googled every item that every kayaker
should have with them.
That was the very first thing that I did.
So there's a beacon that you can get
that you can just press a button
and it immediately lets people know your location,
that would have been great.
- The biggest risk to this case was
falling in the water without a life jacket.
If he'd fallen in the water, he might not have made it
in the cold water without a life jacket.
- I want people to be encouraged to go kayaking
in such a way that they feel also encouraged
to buy these supplies.
That it's not an attack on your adventurous spirit
or your manhood or your pride, like,
these are things that actually make you
feel like you're doing things the right way
because you're very well prepared
and if you were to have loved ones with you,
you wouldn't want to have your pride
get in the way of being very well prepared.
So I mean, we're spending money
on silly things all the time.
If you can afford to go to a movie,
you can afford to get a beacon that's gonna
potentially save your life.
(guitar music)
